message.reasoning:
Gemini's $600 bid for Park Place would leave them with $854 after the purchase, which still needs to cover unmortgaging Boardwalk and building houses for dark blue development—a costly endeavor. I'm reconsidering whether blocking at $601+ is worth it, since my earlier threshold was around $500 max, and this is getting into expensive territory. I'm reconsidering whether to bid $601. At $600 they've already overpaid roughly double, crippling their liquidity to $854 while I keep my full $1500 buffer. Winning at $601 would leave me with only $899 and a useless single Park Place, whereas letting them take it at $600 achieves the same goal—they can't develop dark blue immediately anyway. The math favors dropping out here and preserving my cash position. Looking at what Gemini actually owns—they've got Atlantic and Marvin Gardens from yellow but are missing Ventnor, so that's not an immediate threat. Their only real near-monopoly is dark blue. If I block them here, they stay property-poor and can't develop into a game-ending threat. That reinforces that spending up to $675 is justified to keep them from consolidating power.

But wait—if I let them overpay for Park Place instead, draining them to $854, I'd still have $1500 left to grab Ventnor myself and block their yellow path while weathering their dark blue rent. That might actually be the smarter move since it limits their options across the board rather than just forcing them into one direction.
